issues.description: The specification/UML requires Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return a String ("[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), but the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() as returning boolean and prints the message to stdout instead. This contradicts the described API and breaks the intended usage shown in Main (printing the returned message).
issues.suggestedFix: Change Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String (not boolean) and update Goat/Seal to return "Goat/Seal <name> is milked" without printing. Then Main can print the returned String as described.

issues.description: The template Farm.singFarmSongVerse method has its Animal parameter commented out and therefore has no parameter, while the UML/specification and solution require singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). As-is, students cannot implement singFarmSong() by delegating to a verse method that takes an Animal without changing the method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template signature to `private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)` and add/import the Animal class reference accordingly, matching the UML and solution.

issues.description: The Milkable interface method name and return type are inconsistent with the problem statement/UML: the spec requires Milkable.messageOnMilk(): String (returning "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), but the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk(): boolean and prints the message instead. This breaks student mapping between the required identifier/contract and the provided reference implementation for the same concept.
issues.suggestedFix: Change Milkable to `String messageOnMilk();` and update Goat/Seal implementations to `return "Goat " + getName() + " is milked";` / `return "Seal " + getName() + " is milked";` (remove printing and boolean returns).

issues.description: The setter parameter name for Animal is inconsistent across artifacts: the spec indicates a standard setter (implied `setName(name)`), but the solution uses `setName(String newName)`. This is a minor cross-artifact identifier mismatch for the same conceptual parameter and can cause small confusion when students compare expected signatures with the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the setter parameter to `name` (i.e., `public void setName(String name)`) to match typical expectations and reduce cross-artifact signature comparison friction.
